# The v14 release post leads with the desktop, windows and the team

Owned and due before the Engine 14 cut, so no curated labels.

## Context

The Engine 14 release post (`learn/blog/board-schedule-and-gantt-chart-from-one-engine.md`) reached `dev` with #21043 at `6ed80fc200`, which resolved #21041. The operator read it on 2026-11-23 and gave this direction: the post presents the new components the way a component vendor would. It never mentions the web desktop or that the engine is multi-threaded and multi-window, and it does not show how fast the team built the release or how a peer works. The same read applies to the notes (#22076, PR #22091), and it was sent to their steward.

## The Problem

The post sells the scheduler, the Gantt chart and the board on their features. What sets them apart in Neo is the architecture they run in. The components live in a worker, so one plan can span browser windows. The `shared-planning` example (#22013) shows a scheduler booking, a Gantt task and a board card that are one record, followed across three windows. An agent can edit that plan through the Neural Link. The release's clearest proof of that architecture is missing: a web desktop joins the engine as `Neo.desktop` (#21198), and its windows leave the tab as real browser windows on the same App Worker (#21603, #22067). The team that planned, built and reviewed the release in two weeks gets one closing paragraph.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/worker/Manager.mjs` starts the App, VDom, Data, Task and Canvas workers. With `useSharedWorkers: true` they are SharedWorkers that every window of the app connects to. Both `apps/webdesktop/neo-config.json` and `examples/dashboard/planning/neo-config.json` set it.
- The planning example's docblock (`examples/dashboard/planning/Viewport.mjs`) says: "An opened vessel mounts no second workspace; the shared worker moves the existing pane into its viewport."
- `TaskStore#getBookingStore()` (`src/gantt/TaskStore.mjs`) gives the scheduler and the board a view that borrows the Gantt chart's canonical leaf records.
- First commits of the new families on `dev`: `src/timeline`, `src/scheduler` and `src/gantt` on 2026-11-13, `src/board` on 2026-11-17, `src/desktop` on 2026-11-18. The tear-out merged on the cut day.

## The Fix

Rewrite the post and rename its slug to match. `apps/portal/resources/data/blog.json` is the only other reference. The new order:
1. The hook: drag a window out of the web desktop, and the app keeps running in it.
2. Why it can: the app lives in a worker. A Mermaid diagram shows a main thread per window and the shared workers.
3. The planning families as one plan across windows (`shared-planning`), not as a feature tour.
4. The rest of the release in brief (the server, plain CSS, the catalog), with a link to the notes.
5. The team: how fast, from dated commits and the notes' timestamped counts, and how a peer works, in the author's first person.
6. Try-It: the verified `npx neo-app@14` path, plus the live desktop and planning examples.

Images alternate Neo Dark and Neo Light, from `neomjs/pages` (`webdesktop-14-0.jpg`, `shared-planning-14*.jpg` and the existing Gantt and board frames). The post has no star ask.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The TL;DR and the first section lead with the desktop's tear-out. Multi-threading and multi-window each carry a source anchor.
- [ ] A Mermaid diagram shows the threads and the windows.
- [ ] The planning families appear as one plan across windows.
- [ ] A team section gives the build speed with receipts and how a peer works, in the first person.
- [ ] Images alternate Neo Dark and Neo Light, and the post has no star ask.
- [ ] `blog.json` registers the renamed post and parses.
- [ ] At least two model reviews, one from another family, plus one consolidated fact check by a seat that did not draft the claims.
- [ ] Post-merge: the post renders at reading size on `#/news/blog/<id>`.

## Out of Scope

- The release notes, which stay with #22076's steward.
- The outbound social posts, which follow the merged post.
- New captures.
